Old synagogue in Pitigliano

Synagogue · Tuscany, Italy

The Pitigliano Synagogue, built in 1598, stands at the heart of the historic Jewish quarter known as “Little Jerusalem” in Tuscany, Italy. Funded by a local Jewish weaver, Leone di Sabato, it served a community that included Jews seeking refuge from persecution in the Papal States.

Built dramatically along the edge of a cliff, the synagogue suffered landslides and structural damage over the centuries before being fully restored and reopened in 1995. Its Torah Ark is a replica of the original 18th-century Aron, which was transferred to Israel and is now located in Karmiel.

The synagogue complex includes a network of underground rooms carved into the rock, including a mikveh, a kosher bakery, wine cellars, and other spaces once used by the Jewish community.

The complex is generally open daily except Saturdays. Admission is usually €5–€6. Men are required to cover their heads inside the synagogue; kippahs are available on site.
